title: Directors, Religious Activities and Education
description: Coordinate or design programs and conduct outreach to promote the religious education or activities of a denominational group. May provide counseling, guidance, and leadership relative to marital, health, financial, and religious problems.

tasks.text: Develop or direct study courses or religious education programs within congregations.
Select appropriate curricula or class structures for educational programs.
Schedule special events, such as camps, conferences, meetings, seminars, or retreats.
Collaborate with other ministry members to establish goals and objectives for religious education programs or to develop ways to encourage program participation.
Implement program plans by ordering needed materials, scheduling speakers, reserving space, or handling other administrative details.
Analyze member participation or changes in congregational emphasis to determine needs for religious education.
Attend workshops, seminars, or conferences to obtain program ideas, information, or resources.
Confer with clergy members, congregational officials, or congregational organizations to encourage support of or participation in religious education activities.
Plan fundraising activities for the church.
Plan or conduct conferences dealing with the interpretation of religious ideas or convictions.
Identify and recruit potential volunteer workers.
Counsel individuals regarding interpersonal, health, financial, or religious problems.
Train and supervise religious education instructional staff.
Analyze revenue and program cost data to determine budget priorities.
Visit congregational members' homes or arrange for pastoral visits to provide information or resources regarding religious education programs.
Publicize programs through sources, such as newsletters, bulletins, or mailings.
Interpret religious education activities to the public through speaking, leading discussions, or writing articles for local or national publications.
Locate and distribute resources, such as periodicals or curricula, to enhance the effectiveness of educational programs.
Participate in denominational activities aimed at goals, such as promoting interfaith understanding or providing aid to new or small congregations.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Social Perceptiveness
skills.def: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Critical Thinking
skills.def: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.

skills.name: Active Learning
skills.def: Understanding the implications of new information for both current and future problem-solving and decision-making.

skills.name: Instructing
skills.def: Teaching others how to do something.

skills.name: Service Orientation
skills.def: Actively looking for ways to help people.

skills.name: Learning Strategies
skills.def: Selecting and using training/instructional methods and procedures appropriate for the situation when learning or teaching new things.

skills.name: Coordination
skills.def: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

skills.name: Judgment and Decision Making
skills.def: Considering the relative costs and benefits of potential actions to choose the most appropriate one.

skills.name: Complex Problem Solving
skills.def: Identifying complex problems and reviewing related information to develop and evaluate options and implement solutions.

skills.name: Writing
skills.def: Communicating effectively in writing as appropriate for the needs of the audience.

skills.name: Monitoring

skills.name: Persuasion

skills.name: Systems Analysis

skills.name: Time Management

skills.name: Office suite software
skills.def: Software to provide word processing, spreadsheet, e-mail, presentations, or data management capabilities. Examples: Google Workspace software, Microsoft Office software.

skills.name: Electronic mail software
skills.def: Software to compose, send, or receive email. Examples: Email software, Microsoft Outlook.

skills.name: Spreadsheet software
skills.def: Software to create or edit numbers or text organized into rows and columns of cells. May include formulas which recalculate values based on other cells. Examples: Microsoft Excel.

skills.name: Presentation software
skills.def: Software to create presentations, speeches, or slideshows. Examples: Microsoft PowerPoint.

skills.name: Web page creation and editing software
skills.def: Software to develop or edit web sites or individual pages. Examples: Facebook, Social media software, Website development software.

skills.name: Data base user interface and query software
skills.def: Software to query, present, or edit information stored in a database sytem. Examples: Database software, Microsoft Access.
